edges.description: Loss of lysosomal alpha-NAGA exoglycosidase activity prevents degradation of O-linked glycopeptides and blood-group-A glycoconjugates.
Neuronal glycopeptide and glycoconjugate storage leads to dystrophic axonal spheroid formation and progressive neurodegeneration.
Dystrophic preterminal axonal swelling directly manifests histologically as grey-matter axonal spheroids.
Rapid cortical neurodegeneration causes loss of acquired developmental milestones in infancy.
Rapid cortical neuroaxonal degeneration culminates in profound cognitive impairment in early childhood.
Early central and peripheral neuroaxonal dysfunction presents with infantile hypotonia.
Progressive central and neuromuscular axonal dystrophy causes generalized muscle weakness.
Progressive neuroaxonal degeneration and disuse produce generalized muscle wasting.
Progressive corticospinal tract degeneration produces spasticity and rigidity.
Corticospinal tract neuroaxonal degeneration produces pyramidal tract signs.
Progressive neuroaxonal degeneration is accompanied by loss of deep tendon reflexes.
Progressive neocortical grey-matter degeneration provokes epileptic seizures.
Cortical and subcortical neuroaxonal degeneration produces myoclonic jerks.
Widespread central neuroaxonal degeneration involves brainstem structures.
Progressive visual-pathway neuroaxonal degeneration is accompanied by optic nerve atrophy.
Neocortical visual-pathway neurodegeneration causes cortical visual impairment.
Progressive optic pathway and cerebral visual cortex degeneration culminates in blindness.
Oculomotor and visual-pathway neurodegeneration manifests with nystagmus.
Central oculomotor and visual dysfunction manifests with strabismus.
Progressive auditory pathway neurodegeneration causes sensorineural hearing loss.

nodes.description: Biallelic NAGA loss-of-function variants (such as the E325K substitution, which disrupts the buried E325-R316 salt bridge and destabilizes the homodimeric glycoside hydrolase) abolish lysosomal alpha-N-acetylgalactosaminidase activity required to cleave terminal alpha-N-acetylgalactosamine residues from glycopeptides and glycolipids.

evidence.snippet: Furthermore, transient expression of an alpha-GalNAc construct containing the E325K mutation resulted in the expression of an immunoreactive polypeptide which had no detectable alpha-GalNAc activity.

evidence.reference_title: The 1.9 a structure of human alpha-N-acetylgalactosaminidase: The molecular basis of Schindler and Kanzaki diseases.
evidence.snippet: The E325K substitution leads to the loss of an ion pair between E325 and R316, resulting in the energetically unfavorable clustering of three basic residues (R316, K319, and E325K) within 3 Å of each other.
